message.content:
Here are some of the most famous American composers, spanning classical, popular, and contemporary genres:

| Composer | Lifespan | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|----------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Rodeo* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalist works like *Glassworks*, *Einstein on the Beach*, film scores |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Iconic film scores: *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854–1932) | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “The Washington Post” |
| **Stephen Foster** (1826–1864) | “Oh! Susanna,” “Camptown Races” (American folk/pop classics) |
| **George Frideric Handel** (though German-born, his *Messiah* was premiered in the U.S.) | *Messiah*, *Water Music* (often performed in the U.S.) |

These composers have had a lasting impact on American music, influencing everything from concert halls to Broadway, film, and popular culture.
